name: LM118 / LM218 / LM318 (fast bipolar single op-amp, 15 MHz / 50 V/us)
tagline: Fast 1970s bipolar op-amp (15 MHz, 50 V/us min) that high-slew advocates favoured in the late-70s TIM debate. Now a niche pick for fast buffers and DAC I/V stages.
technology: Bipolar with NPN differential input and an input differential clamp (per LTC SPICE model comments). Internally compensated for unity gain, and external compensation can be added: feed-forward compensation in inverting use gives >150 V/us and nearly double the bandwidth (TI datasheet). Pins 1/5/8 are compensation/balance pins. Single channel, ±5 V to ±20 V supplies.
manufacturers: National Semiconductor (originator of the LM118/LM218/LM318 datasheet line; now TI LM118-N/LM318-N, SNOSBS8)
Texas Instruments (own LM118/LM218/LM318 line, datasheet SLOS063 originally June 1976; also owns ex-National parts since 2011)
Linear Technology (LM318, LM318S8, improved LT118A/LT318A; now Analog Devices) - web-unverified
STMicroelectronics (named in discovery notes only; not verified)

reputation.summary: A fast 1970s bipolar op-amp (15 MHz, 50 V/us min). It is reportedly among the high-slew parts favoured in the late-1970s slew-induced-distortion/TIM debate (Walter Jung et al., Audio magazine), but the specific articles were not verified. Today it is a niche part in DIY circles for fast buffers and DAC I/V stages. Community evidence is thin: there are no published noise specs and no measured reviews were found. It is not a low-noise audio design. Some hobby write-ups wrongly call it a dedicated audio op-amp.
typical_uses: active video filters and video receivers
fast D/A output amplifiers, pulse amplifiers
caveats: High-speed part: bypass pins 4 and 7 with 0.1 uF capacitors placed right at the pins. It is prone to oscillation with stray capacitance on the inverting input and with long socket/adaptor leads.
Pins 1/5/8 are compensation/balance pins, so feed-forward-compensated circuits are not drop-in with parts that use pin 8 as NC or pins 1/5 as offset null.
Feed-forward compensation (>150 V/us) applies only to inverting configurations.
Quiescent current is about 5 mA typ per amp (third-party figure).
No noise specification. Not a low-noise part compared with NE5534/LME49710-class devices.
TI sells two separate LM318 lines (LM318 / SLOS063 and LM318-N / SNOSBS8), and LTC made its own version, so behaviour may differ by maker.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments (TI-legacy) vs National Semiconductor (now TI LM318-N)
silicon_changes.when: Concurrent since 1976 (TI SLOS063 original date) and within the TI catalogue since the 2011 National acquisition
silicon_changes.identification: By datasheet: SLOS063 ('High-Performance Operational Amplifiers', ti.com/product/LM318, lm318.pdf) versus SNOSBS8 ('LM118-N/LM218-N/LM318-N Operational Amplifiers', ti.com/product/LM318-N, lm318-n.pdf). By package code: TI-style D/DR/P/PSR are TI-legacy; National-style N/M/MX/H/J and /NOPB are ex-National.
silicon_changes.summary: TI sells two separately documented LM318 product lines under the same generic number: its own second source (datasheet since June 1976) and National's original (now LM318-N). The die difference is inferred from their separate origins. A third-party audio SPICE modeller also keeps separate National and TI models with different parameters. No vendor document compares the two.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. Compensation, slew and stability margins may differ, so a part swap can change behaviour in fast or feed-forward-compensated circuits.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: same pinout and headline specs (15 MHz, 50 V/us min), but separate designs and datasheets. Check which datasheet (SLOS063 or SNOSBS8) applies to the orderable you buy.
silicon_changes.verification: Not web-searched; second-source differences were outside the priority kinds, and no PCN, die-change or respec claim needed checking.

counterfeit_notes: No specific LM318 counterfeit reports were found. General precaution for cheap marketplace DIP-8 LM318N parts: they may be remarked slower op-amps. As a quick check, run a unity-gain square wave at ±15 V. A genuine part slews at least 50 V/us, while a remarked 741/4558-class part slews under about 1-2 V/us. This is generic advice, not a documented LM318 case. Note also that LM318M (National SOIC) is reported obsolete, so new-stock offers of it deserve extra scrutiny.
alternatives: LME49710 (TI, audio-grade bipolar single; lower slew, much lower noise)
OPA1611 (TI, modern low-noise audio bipolar single)

revision_chain_notes: TI SLOS063 (TI's own LM118/LM218/LM318 line). Known links: original JUNE 1976 (no copy found) -> A, APRIL 1994, titled 'Fast General-Purpose Operational Amplifiers' (copy at pf.unikeyic.com; the already-listed www.unikeyic.com/media copy has the same file hash; the pdf.dzsc.com copy is probably the same edition) -> B, DECEMBER 2002, retitled 'High-Performance Operational Amplifiers' (copies at ti.com lm318.pdf and ti.com/lit/gpn/LM318; the soemtron.org copy has the all-caps Rev B title, so probably Rev B). Missing: any copy of the June 1976 original, and 1970s/80s TI Linear Circuits Data Book editions. National DS007766 (the originator line; figure numbers 007766xx). An edition dated AUGUST 2000 is confirmed by search summary, but which mirror holds it is unknown (candidates: MIT, octopart 92465/9881884, jameco 23608, dokumen.tips, studylib, elcodis, datasheet4u id=1136708). The TI SNOSBS8 header carries 'MARCH 1998', which implies an earlier National DS007766 edition from 1998.
